content.text:
terraria's settings live in the game's own config files on this server, so the ordinary approach is the right one: browse_files from the top of the data directory to find the file that holds the setting, read_file to see it, edit_file to change just that piece, then restart to apply it. Nothing is hidden in the environment on this game, so what you find in those files is the whole picture.

There is no supported way to install mods on terraria through this bot — no registry is wired up for it, so there is nothing to search and nothing to write. Say so plainly. Don't improvise an install by hand through the file tools: anything put there that way is outside everything that would otherwise check it and put it back. If someone wants mods on this game, escalate it as a feature request.

content.text:
The server is fixed and running, and people can connect again at `ev-tr-stuck-starting-s1-cc-opus-1.gameservers.grizzly-endeavors.com:7023`.

**What was wrong:** The server's settings file (`config/serverconfig.txt`) had been changed so the world file name started with a capital letter: `Grizzly.wld`. The file is actually saved as `grizzly.wld`, lowercase. The server treats those as two different names, so it couldn't find the world. It crashed each time it tried to start, and that's why the bot kept saying "starting." An older copy of the settings file still had the lowercase name, so the capital letter was a recent change.

**What I did:**
- **Fixed the name:** I changed it back to `grizzly.wld` and restarted. The world loaded and the server is listening for players.
- **Checked your world:** It was never lost or damaged. The file had been in place the whole time.
- **Made a backup:** The server had no backups at all, so I saved one now that it's working (7.7 MiB). If anything goes wrong later, we can roll back to this point.

**Two other things:**
- The newer settings file is also missing an `autocreate=2` line that the old copy had. That line makes the server generate a new world when it can't find the configured one. I left it out, since your world is there and the server doesn't need it.
- The server log says TShock's first-time setup was never finished. Until it is, the server will keep printing a one-time admin code (`/setup 7195624`). Anyone who joins and types that command first becomes the server's admin. Whoever runs the server should join soon, type it, and follow TShock's prompts to make an admin account.
